headline: Growth accelerates, margins expand as M&A drains cash
summary_short: Thermo Fisher's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 10.5% y/y to $11,994M and GAAP diluted EPS grew 9.3% to $4.68, while adjusted (non-GAAP) EPS grew a faster 13% to $6.03 as GAAP operating margin expanded to 17.4% from 16.9%.
summary_long: Revenue grew 10.5% y/y to $11,994M, comprising 5% organic growth, 5% from acquisitions and 1% currency benefit per the company's own bridge. GAAP operating margin expanded to 17.4% from 16.9% and adjusted operating margin to 22.8% from 21.9%. GAAP diluted EPS rose 9.3% to $4.68; adjusted EPS grew a faster 13% to $6.03. All four segments grew y/y, led by Laboratory Products and Biopharma Services (+11.6%) and Life Sciences Solutions (+12.7%). Cash rose 24.9% q/q to $4,064M even after $8,872M of acquisition spending and $1.0B of Q2 buybacks, funded partly by $5,238M of new debt issuance. Company announced a microbiology-business divestiture; updated FY2026 guidance to be given on the earnings call, not in this release.

drivers.explanation: Growth of 10% comprised 5% organic growth, 5% from acquisitions, and 1% currency translation per the release's own bridge; all four segments grew, led by Laboratory Products and Biopharma Services and Life Sciences Solutions.
GAAP operating margin expanded 50bp to 17.4% from 16.9% as total costs and operating expenses fell to 82.6% of revenue from 83.1%, while revenue grew 10.5%.

GAAP diluted EPS grew 9.3% while adjusted EPS grew faster at 13% to $6.03, since GAAP carries $1.31/share of intangible amortization and other items the adjusted figure excludes per the reconciliation table.
CEO cites the strength of the company's growth strategy, execution and its PPI Business System, saying end markets 'continue to strengthen' and that this is driving continued share gain.

Q2 operating cash flow was $2,125M; the release only discloses investing/financing detail (including $8,872M of acquisition spending, $4,000M of buybacks, $5,238M of new debt issuance) on a six-month, not quarterly, basis.
